title: Overtaking: When and When Not
whatItIs: Overtake only when it is safe and legal to do so. If you are in any doubt, or can't see far enough ahead to be sure, don't overtake.
keyFacts: Before you overtake, make sure the road ahead is clear far enough and nobody is overtaking you.
Overtake on the right. Move back in when it is safe, without cutting in.
You may pass on the left when the vehicle in front is turning right and there is room.
When someone overtakes you, keep a steady speed or slow down. Never speed up.
If a queue builds up behind you, pull in where it is safe and let them pass.

items.title: Bends and hill brows
items.text: Anywhere you can't see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe.

items.title: At or near junctions
items.text: Approaching or at a road junction on either side of the road.

items.title: Near a pedestrian crossing
items.text: You MUST NOT overtake the moving vehicle nearest the crossing, or one stopped for pedestrians.

items.title: Solid white line nearest you
items.text: You MUST NOT cross or straddle it, except in a few cases.

items.title: School crossing patrols
items.text: When approaching a school crossing patrol.

items.title: Level crossings
items.text: Don't overtake at a level crossing.

a.label: Passing on the left: OK
points: Queues where your lane is faster

b.label: Passing on the left: no
points: To get past a slow driver
Moving left on a motorway to overtake

onTheTest.question: Another vehicle is overtaking you. What should you do?
options: Keep a steady speed, or slow down
Speed up to stop them passing
Move towards the middle of the road
Brake hard to let them in
onTheTest.why: Keep a steady speed and slow down if needed to let them back in safely. Speeding up puts everyone at risk.

traps: A broken centre line doesn't make it safe near junctions, bends or hill brows.
A vehicle signalling right may be about to turn: never pass it on the right.
Being overtaken? Speeding up is dangerous and aggressive.
